Structural cleanup of the video-editor selection store API.

# Background

We just landed a 3-line quick fix on branch `megaplan/m1b-m1c-stores` that removes redundant double-writes from `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineSelection.ts`. The wrapper was calling both the store action AND a `setSelectedClipId` pass-through that routed to `setTimelineSelectedClipId` → `selectTimelineClip(id, undefined)`, which silently reset multi-select to single-select. Marquee + cmd+click multi-select are now functional.

The bug is fixed but the underlying smell that produced it is intact: the selection store has three overlapping entry points with subtly-different semantics, one of which (`setTimelineSelectedClipId`) masquerades as a `useState` setter while actually clobbering the whole selection. The wrapper layer (`useTimelineSelection`) still has the pre-refactor "split state" shape (multi-select set + useState-style primary id) even though M1b/M1c collapsed those into a single Zustand store.

# Goal

Eliminate the structural trap permanently so this class of bug cannot reappear, even if a future refactor wires the surfaces back together. This megaplan plans the cleanup ONLY — the bug fix is already applied. The cleanup should ship in the same PR as the quick fix but as a separate commit so the fix is revertable independently.

# Specific objectives

1. **Disambiguate the three entry points** in `src/shared/state/selectionStore.ts`:
   - `selectTimelineClips(set, syncOptions)` — replaces multi-selection
   - `selectTimelineClip(id, opts, syncOptions)` — single or toggle
   - `setTimelineSelectedClipId(updater, options)` — masquerades as primary-id setter, actually resets selection. **THIS IS THE TRAP.**

   Either rename `setTimelineSelectedClipId` so it stops looking like a `useState` setter, or split it into `setPrimaryClipId` (pure primary update, no reset) + `selectSingleClip` (replaces selection with one). Pick whichever leaves the cleanest contract for callers.

2. **Decide the fate of `useTimelineSelection`**. Post-M1b/M1c, the wrapper is a thin layer over the store but still presents `Dispatch<SetStateAction<string | null>>` semantics. Options:
   - Kill it; have callers use the store hooks directly.
   - Thin it to JUST derivations (`selectedClip`, `selectedTrack`, `selectedClipHasPredecessor`, `resolvedConfig` from `useDerivedTimeline`) and drop all selection-mutation methods.

3. **Update `useTimelineCommit.ts:117`**. This is where `setSelectedClipId` is created with the deceptive setState-style signature. It needs to either disappear (callers go direct) or be renamed to match the new contract.

4. **Document semantics inline** so the next refactor doesn't reintroduce the trap. JSDoc on each store action stating exactly what it resets and what it preserves.

# Constraints / context

- **Branch**: `megaplan/m1b-m1c-stores` (not yet merged; itself a major refactor moving selection from React Context into Zustand stores).
- **User confirmed they are happy with churn** — broad renames and call-site updates are acceptable.
- **Test files affected** (~6+): `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipEditing.test.ts`, `src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/ClipAction.test.tsx`, and others mocking `setSelectedClipId: vi.fn()`.

## Adjacent flows the planner MUST check for hidden coupling

These flows touch selection and may rely on the side effects of the current double-write or the setState-style signature. The plan must verify each:

- **Gallery sync** (`clearGallery` options on store actions). Some callers pass `{clearGallery: false}` — if those reach a renamed/split API, the option must survive.
- **Lightbox navigation** — `MediaLightbox` interaction with selection state.
- **Agent chat ops** — `AgentChatContext` and `AgentChat` reference selection (per the modified files in working tree).
- **Programmatic post-creation selection** — select-after-paste, select-after-shot-creation, select-after-clip-duplication. Often uses `setSelectedClipId(newId)` semantics.
- **`useClipDrag` pointer-up** — calls `selectClip(id, {toggle, preserveSelection})` based on modifier keys and touch interaction.
- **`useMarqueeSelect`** — calls `selectClips`, `addToSelection`, `clearSelection`.
- **`useAssetManagement`** — passes `setSelectedClipId` through.

## Files in the surface area (not exhaustive)

- `src/shared/state/selectionStore.ts` — the store (where the renames land)
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineSelection.ts` — the wrapper (kill or thin)
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineCommit.ts:117` — the bridge (likely the surface to rename or remove)
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineState.ts` — composes selection into editor state
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipDrag.ts` — call site
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useMarqueeSelect.ts` — call site
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useAssetManagement.ts` — call site
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipEditing.ts` — call site
- `src/tools/video-editor/contexts/VideoEditorProvider.tsx` — composes ops into the timelineStore
- All test files that mock these APIs

Either may already exist (State A) or both may be in the worktree (State B). T1 resolves this; do NOT carry the ambiguity past T1.\n\nThe single load-bearing invariant: `useTimelineMultiSelect`'s `{clearGallery: false}` adapter at `selectionStore.ts:780-789` MUST stay. It preserves gallery selection during editor-internal mutations (drag, marquee, programmatic post-creation selects). The cleanup ONLY removes the trap method (`setSelectedClipId` field on the hook surface and the underlying `setTimelineSelectedClipId` action) \u2014 not the surrounding wrappers. If the post-cleanup smoke shows that clicking a timeline clip clears gallery selection, T2 was misapplied (the adapter was deleted with the trap).\n\nThe most subtle correctness point is the gallery-default asymmetry: `clearTimelineSelection` PRESERVES gallery by default (opt-IN to clear), opposite to `selectTimelineClip`/`selectTimelineClips` which CLEAR gallery by default (opt-OUT). The JSDoc on `clearTimelineSelection` must state this as a 'Note: opposite gallery default' callout \u2014 boilerplate that papers over the divergence would seed the same kind of misreading that produced the original trap. The plan deliberately does NOT normalize this asymmetry; that is a behavior-change PR.\n\n`useTimelineCommit.ts:190` keeps an explicit `{clearGallery: false}` even though it is functionally redundant with `clearTimelineSelection`'s default. This is intentional readability \u2014 a reader scanning the commit hook sees the same `{clearGallery: false}` keyword on every editor-internal selection write. Resist 'cleaning up' the redundancy.\n\n`setSelectedTrackId` is the lookalike trap \u2014 it ISN'T a trap because track selection is a single scalar with no multi-select to clobber. Keep it untouched. Do NOT use a broad grep pattern that catches it; use `\\\\bsetSelectedClipId\\\\b` precisely.\n\nOVERLAP_FILES staging is the most failure-prone part of execution. The user is mid-stream on a pane-refactor bakeoff with entangled changes across many files; `git stash` is NOT safe here. # Background

We just landed a 3-line quick fix on branch `megaplan/m1b-m1c-stores` that removes redundant double-writes from `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineSelection.ts`. The wrapper was calling both the store action AND a `setSelectedClipId` pass-through that routed to `setTimelineSelectedClipId` → `selectTimelineClip(id, undefined)`, which silently reset multi-select to single-select. Marquee + cmd+click multi-select are now functional.

The bug is fixed but the underlying smell that produced it is intact: the selection store has three overlapping entry points with subtly-different semantics, one of which (`setTimelineSelectedClipId`) masquerades as a `useState` setter while actually clobbering the whole selection. The wrapper layer (`useTimelineSelection`) still has the pre-refactor "split state" shape (multi-select set + useState-style primary id) even though M1b/M1c collapsed those into a single Zustand store.

# Goal

Eliminate the structural trap permanently so this class of bug cannot reappear, even if a future refactor wires the surfaces back together. This megaplan plans the cleanup ONLY — the bug fix is already applied. The cleanup should ship in the same PR as the quick fix but as a separate commit so the fix is revertable independently.

# Specific objectives

1. **Disambiguate the three entry points** in `src/shared/state/selectionStore.ts`:
   - `selectTimelineClips(set, syncOptions)` — replaces multi-selection
   - `selectTimelineClip(id, opts, syncOptions)` — single or toggle
   - `setTimelineSelectedClipId(updater, options)` — masquerades as primary-id setter, actually resets selection. **THIS IS THE TRAP.**

   Either rename `setTimelineSelectedClipId` so it stops looking like a `useState` setter, or split it into `setPrimaryClipId` (pure primary update, no reset) + `selectSingleClip` (replaces selection with one). Pick whichever leaves the cleanest contract for callers.

2. **Decide the fate of `useTimelineSelection`**. Post-M1b/M1c, the wrapper is a thin layer over the store but still presents `Dispatch<SetStateAction<string | null>>` semantics. Options:
   - Kill it; have callers use the store hooks directly.
   - Thin it to JUST derivations (`selectedClip`, `selectedTrack`, `selectedClipHasPredecessor`, `resolvedConfig` from `useDerivedTimeline`) and drop all selection-mutation methods.

3. **Update `useTimelineCommit.ts:117`**. This is where `setSelectedClipId` is created with the deceptive setState-style signature. It needs to either disappear (callers go direct) or be renamed to match the new contract.

4. **Document semantics inline** so the next refactor doesn't reintroduce the trap. JSDoc on each store action stating exactly what it resets and what it preserves.

# Constraints / context

- **Branch**: `megaplan/m1b-m1c-stores` (not yet merged; itself a major refactor moving selection from React Context into Zustand stores).
- **User confirmed they are happy with churn** — broad renames and call-site updates are acceptable.
- **Test files affected** (~6+): `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipEditing.test.ts`, `src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/ClipAction.test.tsx`, and others mocking `setSelectedClipId: vi.fn()`.

## Adjacent flows the planner MUST check for hidden coupling

These flows touch selection and may rely on the side effects of the current double-write or the setState-style signature. The plan must verify each:

- **Gallery sync** (`clearGallery` options on store actions). Some callers pass `{clearGallery: false}` — if those reach a renamed/split API, the option must survive.
- **Lightbox navigation** — `MediaLightbox` interaction with selection state.
- **Agent chat ops** — `AgentChatContext` and `AgentChat` reference selection (per the modified files in working tree).
- **Programmatic post-creation selection** — select-after-paste, select-after-shot-creation, select-after-clip-duplication. Often uses `setSelectedClipId(newId)` semantics.
- **`useClipDrag` pointer-up** — calls `selectClip(id, {toggle, preserveSelection})` based on modifier keys and touch interaction.
- **`useMarqueeSelect`** — calls `selectClips`, `addToSelection`, `clearSelection`.
- **`useAssetManagement`** — passes `setSelectedClipId` through.

## Files in the surface area (not exhaustive)

- `src/shared/state/selectionStore.ts` — the store (where the renames land)
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineSelection.ts` — the wrapper (kill or thin)
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineCommit.ts:117` — the bridge (likely the surface to rename or remove)
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineState.ts` — composes selection into editor state
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipDrag.ts` — call site
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useMarqueeSelect.ts` — call site
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useAssetManagement.ts` — call site
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipEditing.ts` — call site
- `src/tools/video-editor/contexts/VideoEditorProvider.tsx` — composes ops into the timelineStore
- All test files that mock these APIs

# What I want from this plan

1. **Map the current API surface and EVERY call site** (don't trust my partial list — search the whole repo).
2. **Propose a target API** with exact names and signatures. Justify the choice (split vs single rename).
3. **Sequence the migration into reviewable chunks** — ideally each chunk leaves the build green.
4. **Identify load-bearing side effects** of the current double-write — places where the second write was the actual intended behavior, not a bug.
5. **Identify adjacent-flow verification points** — what to manually test (gallery, lightbox, agent chat, post-creation selection, drag-after-multi-select).
6. **List every test file that will need updating** and what kind of update (mock signature change, behavior assertion change, etc.).

  "meta_commentary": "This cleanup ships in TWO commits on `megaplan/m1b-m1c-stores`: (1) the 3-line bug fix `fix(selection): remove double-write that clobbers multi-select` and (2) the structural cleanup `refactor(selection): remove setTimelineSelectedClipId trap`. Either may already exist (State A) or both may be in the worktree (State B). T1 resolves this; do NOT carry the ambiguity past T1.\n\nThe single load-bearing invariant: `useTimelineMultiSelect`'s `{clearGallery: false}` adapter at `selectionStore.ts:780-789` MUST stay. It preserves gallery selection during editor-internal mutations (drag, marquee, programmatic post-creation selects). The cleanup ONLY removes the trap method (`setSelectedClipId` field on the hook surface and the underlying `setTimelineSelectedClipId` action) \u2014 not the surrounding wrappers. If the post-cleanup smoke shows that clicking a timeline clip clears gallery selection, T2 was misapplied (the adapter was deleted with the trap).\n\nThe most subtle correctness point is the gallery-default asymmetry: `clearTimelineSelection` PRESERVES gallery by default (opt-IN to clear), opposite to `selectTimelineClip`/`selectTimelineClips` which CLEAR gallery by default (opt-OUT). The JSDoc on `clearTimelineSelection` must state this as a 'Note: opposite gallery default' callout \u2014 boilerplate that papers over the divergence would seed the same kind of misreading that produced the original trap. The plan deliberately does NOT normalize this asymmetry; that is a behavior-change PR.\n\n`useTimelineCommit.ts:190` keeps an explicit `{clearGallery: false}` even though it is functionally redundant with `clearTimelineSelection`'s default. This is intentional readability \u2014 a reader scanning the commit hook sees the same `{clearGallery: false}` keyword on every editor-internal selection write. Resist 'cleaning up' the redundancy.\n\n`setSelectedTrackId` is the lookalike trap \u2014 it ISN'T a trap because track selection is a single scalar with no multi-select to clobber. Keep it untouched. Do NOT use a broad grep pattern that catches it; use `\\\\bsetSelectedClipId\\\\b` precisely.\n\nOVERLAP_FILES staging is the most failure-prone part of execution. The user is mid-stream on a pane-refactor bakeoff with entangled changes across many files; `git stash` is NOT safe here. Use `git add -p <path>` for every overlap file, then `git diff --cached -- <path>` per overlap file before commit. If foreign hunks slip in, `git restore --staged <path>` and redo. The path-only `git status --short` check is necessary but insufficient \u2014 the per-overlap-file diff review is the load-bearing protection.\n\n`useAssetManagement.ts` is easy to half-migrate. The prop AND the store-backed resolver (`getSetSelectedClipId` \u2192 `getSelectClip` reading `ops.selectClip`) MUST move together. Missing the store-backed path silently breaks post-paste / post-creation selection at runtime even though the build passes.\n\nValidation cadence (matches plan): tsc after T4 (Phase 1-2 done), tsc after T8 (Phase 4 done), tsc after T11 (Phase 5 done), then full vitest + grep + manual smoke after T12. Do not skip the intermediate tsc runs \u2014 they catch broken consumers cheaply before the test suite has to.",

        Idea:
Structural cleanup of the video-editor selection store API.

# Background

We just landed a 3-line quick fix on branch `megaplan/m1b-m1c-stores` that removes redundant double-writes from `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineSelection.ts`. The wrapper was calling both the store action AND a `setSelectedClipId` pass-through that routed to `setTimelineSelectedClipId` → `selectTimelineClip(id, undefined)`, which silently reset multi-select to single-select. Marquee + cmd+click multi-select are now functional.

The bug is fixed but the underlying smell that produced it is intact: the selection store has three overlapping entry points with subtly-different semantics, one of which (`setTimelineSelectedClipId`) masquerades as a `useState` setter while actually clobbering the whole selection. The wrapper layer (`useTimelineSelection`) still has the pre-refactor "split state" shape (multi-select set + useState-style primary id) even though M1b/M1c collapsed those into a single Zustand store.

# Goal

Eliminate the structural trap permanently so this class of bug cannot reappear, even if a future refactor wires the surfaces back together. This megaplan plans the cleanup ONLY — the bug fix is already applied. The cleanup should ship in the same PR as the quick fix but as a separate commit so the fix is revertable independently.

# Specific objectives

1. **Disambiguate the three entry points** in `src/shared/state/selectionStore.ts`:
   - `selectTimelineClips(set, syncOptions)` — replaces multi-selection
   - `selectTimelineClip(id, opts, syncOptions)` — single or toggle
   - `setTimelineSelectedClipId(updater, options)` — masquerades as primary-id setter, actually resets selection. **THIS IS THE TRAP.**

   Either rename `setTimelineSelectedClipId` so it stops looking like a `useState` setter, or split it into `setPrimaryClipId` (pure primary update, no reset) + `selectSingleClip` (replaces selection with one). Pick whichever leaves the cleanest contract for callers.

2. **Decide the fate of `useTimelineSelection`**. Post-M1b/M1c, the wrapper is a thin layer over the store but still presents `Dispatch<SetStateAction<string | null>>` semantics. Options:
   - Kill it; have callers use the store hooks directly.
   - Thin it to JUST derivations (`selectedClip`, `selectedTrack`, `selectedClipHasPredecessor`, `resolvedConfig` from `useDerivedTimeline`) and drop all selection-mutation methods.

3. **Update `useTimelineCommit.ts:117`**. This is where `setSelectedClipId` is created with the deceptive setState-style signature. It needs to either disappear (callers go direct) or be renamed to match the new contract.

4. **Document semantics inline** so the next refactor doesn't reintroduce the trap. JSDoc on each store action stating exactly what it resets and what it preserves.

# Constraints / context

- **Branch**: `megaplan/m1b-m1c-stores` (not yet merged; itself a major refactor moving selection from React Context into Zustand stores).
- **User confirmed they are happy with churn** — broad renames and call-site updates are acceptable.
- **Test files affected** (~6+): `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipEditing.test.ts`, `src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/ClipAction.test.tsx`, and others mocking `setSelectedClipId: vi.fn()`.

## Adjacent flows the planner MUST check for hidden coupling

These flows touch selection and may rely on the side effects of the current double-write or the setState-style signature. The plan must verify each:

- **Gallery sync** (`clearGallery` options on store actions). Some callers pass `{clearGallery: false}` — if those reach a renamed/split API, the option must survive.
- **Lightbox navigation** — `MediaLightbox` interaction with selection state.
- **Agent chat ops** — `AgentChatContext` and `AgentChat` reference selection (per the modified files in working tree).
- **Programmatic post-creation selection** — select-after-paste, select-after-shot-creation, select-after-clip-duplication. Often uses `setSelectedClipId(newId)` semantics.
- **`useClipDrag` pointer-up** — calls `selectClip(id, {toggle, preserveSelection})` based on modifier keys and touch interaction.
- **`useMarqueeSelect`** — calls `selectClips`, `addToSelection`, `clearSelection`.
- **`useAssetManagement`** — passes `setSelectedClipId` through.

## Files in the surface area (not exhaustive)

- `src/shared/state/selectionStore.ts` — the store (where the renames land)
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineSelection.ts` — the wrapper (kill or thin)
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineCommit.ts:117` — the bridge (likely the surface to rename or remove)
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineState.ts` — composes selection into editor state
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipDrag.ts` — call site
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useMarqueeSelect.ts` — call site
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useAssetManagement.ts` — call site
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipEditing.ts` — call site
- `src/tools/video-editor/contexts/VideoEditorProvider.tsx` — composes ops into the timelineStore
- All test files that mock these APIs

# What I want from this plan

1. **Map the current API surface and EVERY call site** (don't trust my partial list — search the whole repo).
2. **Propose a target API** with exact names and signatures. Justify the choice (split vs single rename).
3. **Sequence the migration into reviewable chunks** — ideally each chunk leaves the build green.
4. **Identify load-bearing side effects** of the current double-write — places where the second write was the actual intended behavior, not a bug.
5. **Identify adjacent-flow verification points** — what to manually test (gallery, lightbox, agent chat, post-creation selection, drag-after-multi-select).
6. **List every test file that will need updating** and what kind of update (mock signature change, behavior assertion change, etc.).

T1 resolves this; do NOT carry the ambiguity past T1.\n\nThe single load-bearing invariant: `useTimelineMultiSelect`'s `{clearGallery: false}` adapter at `selectionStore.ts:780-789` MUST stay. It preserves gallery selection during editor-internal mutations (drag, marquee, programmatic post-creation selects). The cleanup ONLY removes the trap method (`setSelectedClipId` field on the hook surface and the underlying `setTimelineSelectedClipId` action) \u2014 not the surrounding wrappers. If the post-cleanup smoke shows that clicking a timeline clip clears gallery selection, T2 was misapplied (the adapter was deleted with the trap).\n\nThe most subtle correctness point is the gallery-default asymmetry: `clearTimelineSelection` PRESERVES gallery by default (opt-IN to clear), opposite to `selectTimelineClip`/`selectTimelineClips` which CLEAR gallery by default (opt-OUT). The JSDoc on `clearTimelineSelection` must state this as a 'Note: opposite gallery default' callout \u2014 boilerplate that papers over the divergence would seed the same kind of misreading that produced the original trap. The plan deliberately does NOT normalize this asymmetry; that is a behavior-change PR.\n\n`useTimelineCommit.ts:190` keeps an explicit `{clearGallery: false}` even though it is functionally redundant with `clearTimelineSelection`'s default. This is intentional readability \u2014 a reader scanning the commit hook sees the same `{clearGallery: false}` keyword on every editor-internal selection write. Resist 'cleaning up' the redundancy.\n\n`setSelectedTrackId` is the lookalike trap \u2014 it ISN'T a trap because track selection is a single scalar with no multi-select to clobber. Keep it untouched. Do NOT use a broad grep pattern that catches it; use `\\\\bsetSelectedClipId\\\\b` precisely.\n\nOVERLAP_FILES staging is the most failure-prone part of execution. The user is mid-stream on a pane-refactor bakeoff with entangled changes across many files; `git stash` is NOT safe here. Use `git add -p <path>` for every overlap file, then `git diff --cached -- <path>` per overlap file before commit. If foreign hunks slip in, `git restore --staged <path>` and redo. The path-only `git status --short` check is necessary but insufficient \u2014 the per-overlap-file diff review is the load-bearing protection.\n\n`useAssetManagement.ts` is easy to half-migrate. The prop AND the store-backed resolver (`getSetSelectedClipId` \u2192 `getSelectClip` reading `ops.selectClip`) MUST move together. Missing the store-backed path silently breaks post-paste / post-creation selection at runtime even though the build passes.\n\nValidation cadence (matches plan): tsc after T4 (Phase 1-2 done), tsc after T8 (Phase 4 done), tsc after T11 (Phase 5 done), then full vitest + grep + manual smoke after T12. Do not skip the intermediate tsc runs \u2014 they catch broken consumers cheaply before the test suite has to.",

        Idea:
Structural cleanup of the video-editor selection store API.

# Background

We just landed a 3-line quick fix on branch `megaplan/m1b-m1c-stores` that removes redundant double-writes from `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineSelection.ts`. The wrapper was calling both the store action AND a `setSelectedClipId` pass-through that routed to `setTimelineSelectedClipId` → `selectTimelineClip(id, undefined)`, which silently reset multi-select to single-select. Marquee + cmd+click multi-select are now functional.

The bug is fixed but the underlying smell that produced it is intact: the selection store has three overlapping entry points with subtly-different semantics, one of which (`setTimelineSelectedClipId`) masquerades as a `useState` setter while actually clobbering the whole selection. The wrapper layer (`useTimelineSelection`) still has the pre-refactor "split state" shape (multi-select set + useState-style primary id) even though M1b/M1c collapsed those into a single Zustand store.

# Goal

Eliminate the structural trap permanently so this class of bug cannot reappear, even if a future refactor wires the surfaces back together. This megaplan plans the cleanup ONLY — the bug fix is already applied. The cleanup should ship in the same PR as the quick fix but as a separate commit so the fix is revertable independently.

# Specific objectives

1. **Disambiguate the three entry points** in `src/shared/state/selectionStore.ts`:
   - `selectTimelineClips(set, syncOptions)` — replaces multi-selection
   - `selectTimelineClip(id, opts, syncOptions)` — single or toggle
   - `setTimelineSelectedClipId(updater, options)` — masquerades as primary-id setter, actually resets selection. **THIS IS THE TRAP.**

   Either rename `setTimelineSelectedClipId` so it stops looking like a `useState` setter, or split it into `setPrimaryClipId` (pure primary update, no reset) + `selectSingleClip` (replaces selection with one). Pick whichever leaves the cleanest contract for callers.

2. **Decide the fate of `useTimelineSelection`**. Post-M1b/M1c, the wrapper is a thin layer over the store but still presents `Dispatch<SetStateAction<string | null>>` semantics. Options:
   - Kill it; have callers use the store hooks directly.
   - Thin it to JUST derivations (`selectedClip`, `selectedTrack`, `selectedClipHasPredecessor`, `resolvedConfig` from `useDerivedTimeline`) and drop all selection-mutation methods.

3. **Update `useTimelineCommit.ts:117`**. This is where `setSelectedClipId` is created with the deceptive setState-style signature. It needs to either disappear (callers go direct) or be renamed to match the new contract.

4. **Document semantics inline** so the next refactor doesn't reintroduce the trap. JSDoc on each store action stating exactly what it resets and what it preserves.

# Constraints / context

- **Branch**: `megaplan/m1b-m1c-stores` (not yet merged; itself a major refactor moving selection from React Context into Zustand stores).
- **User confirmed they are happy with churn** — broad renames and call-site updates are acceptable.
- **Test files affected** (~6+): `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipEditing.test.ts`, `src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/ClipAction.test.tsx`, and others mocking `setSelectedClipId: vi.fn()`.

## Adjacent flows the planner MUST check for hidden coupling

These flows touch selection and may rely on the side effects of the current double-write or the setState-style signature. The plan must verify each:

- **Gallery sync** (`clearGallery` options on store actions). Some callers pass `{clearGallery: false}` — if those reach a renamed/split API, the option must survive.
- **Lightbox navigation** — `MediaLightbox` interaction with selection state.
- **Agent chat ops** — `AgentChatContext` and `AgentChat` reference selection (per the modified files in working tree).
- **Programmatic post-creation selection** — select-after-paste, select-after-shot-creation, select-after-clip-duplication. Often uses `setSelectedClipId(newId)` semantics.
- **`useClipDrag` pointer-up** — calls `selectClip(id, {toggle, preserveSelection})` based on modifier keys and touch interaction.
- **`useMarqueeSelect`** — calls `selectClips`, `addToSelection`, `clearSelection`.
- **`useAssetManagement`** — passes `setSelectedClipId` through.

## Files in the surface area (not exhaustive)

- `src/shared/state/selectionStore.ts` — the store (where the renames land)
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineSelection.ts` — the wrapper (kill or thin)
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineCommit.ts:117` — the bridge (likely the surface to rename or remove)
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineState.ts` — composes selection into editor state
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipDrag.ts` — call site
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useMarqueeSelect.ts` — call site
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useAssetManagement.ts` — call site
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipEditing.ts` — call site
- `src/tools/video-editor/contexts/VideoEditorProvider.tsx` — composes ops into the timelineStore
- All test files that mock these APIs

# What I want from this plan

1. **Map the current API surface and EVERY call site** (don't trust my partial list — search the whole repo).
2. **Propose a target API** with exact names and signatures. Justify the choice (split vs single rename).
3. **Sequence the migration into reviewable chunks** — ideally each chunk leaves the build green.
4. **Identify load-bearing side effects** of the current double-write — places where the second write was the actual intended behavior, not a bug.
5. **Identify adjacent-flow verification points** — what to manually test (gallery, lightbox, agent chat, post-creation selection, drag-after-multi-select).
6. **List every test file that will need updating** and what kind of update (mock signature change, behavior assertion change, etc.).

  "meta_commentary": "This cleanup ships in TWO commits on `megaplan/m1b-m1c-stores`: (1) the 3-line bug fix `fix(selection): remove double-write that clobbers multi-select` and (2) the structural cleanup `refactor(selection): remove setTimelineSelectedClipId trap`. Either may already exist (State A) or both may be in the worktree (State B). T1 resolves this; do NOT carry the ambiguity past T1.\n\nThe single load-bearing invariant: `useTimelineMultiSelect`'s `{clearGallery: false}` adapter at `selectionStore.ts:780-789` MUST stay. It preserves gallery selection during editor-internal mutations (drag, marquee, programmatic post-creation selects). The cleanup ONLY removes the trap method (`setSelectedClipId` field on the hook surface and the underlying `setTimelineSelectedClipId` action) \u2014 not the surrounding wrappers. If the post-cleanup smoke shows that clicking a timeline clip clears gallery selection, T2 was misapplied (the adapter was deleted with the trap).\n\nThe most subtle correctness point is the gallery-default asymmetry: `clearTimelineSelection` PRESERVES gallery by default (opt-IN to clear), opposite to `selectTimelineClip`/`selectTimelineClips` which CLEAR gallery by default (opt-OUT). The JSDoc on `clearTimelineSelection` must state this as a 'Note: opposite gallery default' callout \u2014 boilerplate that papers over the divergence would seed the same kind of misreading that produced the original trap. The plan deliberately does NOT normalize this asymmetry; that is a behavior-change PR.\n\n`useTimelineCommit.ts:190` keeps an explicit `{clearGallery: false}` even though it is functionally redundant with `clearTimelineSelection`'s default. This is intentional readability \u2014 a reader scanning the commit hook sees the same `{clearGallery: false}` keyword on every editor-internal selection write. Resist 'cleaning up' the redundancy.\n\n`setSelectedTrackId` is the lookalike trap \u2014 it ISN'T a trap because track selection is a single scalar with no multi-select to clobber. Keep it untouched. Do NOT use a broad grep pattern that catches it; use `\\\\bsetSelectedClipId\\\\b` precisely.\n\nOVERLAP_FILES staging is the most failure-prone part of execution. The user is mid-stream on a pane-refactor bakeoff with entangled changes across many files; `git stash` is NOT safe here. Use `git add -p <path>` for every overlap file, then `git diff --cached -- <path>` per overlap file before commit. If foreign hunks slip in, `git restore --staged <path>` and redo. The path-only `git status --short` check is necessary but insufficient \u2014 the per-overlap-file diff review is the load-bearing protection.\n\n`useAssetManagement.ts` is easy to half-migrate. The prop AND the store-backed resolver (`getSetSelectedClipId` \u2192 `getSelectClip` reading `ops.selectClip`) MUST move together. Missing the store-backed path silently breaks post-paste / post-creation selection at runtime even though the build passes.\n\nValidation cadence (matches plan): tsc after T4 (Phase 1-2 done), tsc after T8 (Phase 4 done), tsc after T11 (Phase 5 done), then full vitest + grep + manual smoke after T12.         Idea:
Structural cleanup of the video-editor selection store API.

# Background

We just landed a 3-line quick fix on branch `megaplan/m1b-m1c-stores` that removes redundant double-writes from `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineSelection.ts`. The wrapper was calling both the store action AND a `setSelectedClipId` pass-through that routed to `setTimelineSelectedClipId` → `selectTimelineClip(id, undefined)`, which silently reset multi-select to single-select. Marquee + cmd+click multi-select are now functional.

The bug is fixed but the underlying smell that produced it is intact: the selection store has three overlapping entry points with subtly-different semantics, one of which (`setTimelineSelectedClipId`) masquerades as a `useState` setter while actually clobbering the whole selection. The wrapper layer (`useTimelineSelection`) still has the pre-refactor "split state" shape (multi-select set + useState-style primary id) even though M1b/M1c collapsed those into a single Zustand store.

# Goal

Eliminate the structural trap permanently so this class of bug cannot reappear, even if a future refactor wires the surfaces back together. This megaplan plans the cleanup ONLY — the bug fix is already applied. The cleanup should ship in the same PR as the quick fix but as a separate commit so the fix is revertable independently.

# Specific objectives

1. **Disambiguate the three entry points** in `src/shared/state/selectionStore.ts`:
   - `selectTimelineClips(set, syncOptions)` — replaces multi-selection
   - `selectTimelineClip(id, opts, syncOptions)` — single or toggle
   - `setTimelineSelectedClipId(updater, options)` — masquerades as primary-id setter, actually resets selection. **THIS IS THE TRAP.**

   Either rename `setTimelineSelectedClipId` so it stops looking like a `useState` setter, or split it into `setPrimaryClipId` (pure primary update, no reset) + `selectSingleClip` (replaces selection with one). Pick whichever leaves the cleanest contract for callers.

2. **Decide the fate of `useTimelineSelection`**. Post-M1b/M1c, the wrapper is a thin layer over the store but still presents `Dispatch<SetStateAction<string | null>>` semantics. Options:
   - Kill it; have callers use the store hooks directly.
   - Thin it to JUST derivations (`selectedClip`, `selectedTrack`, `selectedClipHasPredecessor`, `resolvedConfig` from `useDerivedTimeline`) and drop all selection-mutation methods.

3. **Update `useTimelineCommit.ts:117`**. This is where `setSelectedClipId` is created with the deceptive setState-style signature. It needs to either disappear (callers go direct) or be renamed to match the new contract.

4. **Document semantics inline** so the next refactor doesn't reintroduce the trap. JSDoc on each store action stating exactly what it resets and what it preserves.

# Constraints / context

- **Branch**: `megaplan/m1b-m1c-stores` (not yet merged; itself a major refactor moving selection from React Context into Zustand stores).
- **User confirmed they are happy with churn** — broad renames and call-site updates are acceptable.
- **Test files affected** (~6+): `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipEditing.test.ts`, `src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/ClipAction.test.tsx`, and others mocking `setSelectedClipId: vi.fn()`.

## Adjacent flows the planner MUST check for hidden coupling

These flows touch selection and may rely on the side effects of the current double-write or the setState-style signature. The plan must verify each:

- **Gallery sync** (`clearGallery` options on store actions). Some callers pass `{clearGallery: false}` — if those reach a renamed/split API, the option must survive.
- **Lightbox navigation** — `MediaLightbox` interaction with selection state.
- **Agent chat ops** — `AgentChatContext` and `AgentChat` reference selection (per the modified files in working tree).
- **Programmatic post-creation selection** — select-after-paste, select-after-shot-creation, select-after-clip-duplication. Often uses `setSelectedClipId(newId)` semantics.
- **`useClipDrag` pointer-up** — calls `selectClip(id, {toggle, preserveSelection})` based on modifier keys and touch interaction.
- **`useMarqueeSelect`** — calls `selectClips`, `addToSelection`, `clearSelection`.
- **`useAssetManagement`** — passes `setSelectedClipId` through.

## Files in the surface area (not exhaustive)

- `src/shared/state/selectionStore.ts` — the store (where the renames land)
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineSelection.ts` — the wrapper (kill or thin)
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineCommit.ts:117` — the bridge (likely the surface to rename or remove)
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineState.ts` — composes selection into editor state
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipDrag.ts` — call site
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useMarqueeSelect.ts` — call site
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useAssetManagement.ts` — call site
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipEditing.ts` — call site
- `src/tools/video-editor/contexts/VideoEditorProvider.tsx` — composes ops into the timelineStore
- All test files that mock these APIs

# What I want from this plan

1. **Map the current API surface and EVERY call site** (don't trust my partial list — search the whole repo).
2. **Propose a target API** with exact names and signatures. Justify the choice (split vs single rename).
3. **Sequence the migration into reviewable chunks** — ideally each chunk leaves the build green.
4. **Identify load-bearing side effects** of the current double-write — places where the second write was the actual intended behavior, not a bug.
5. **Identify adjacent-flow verification points** — what to manually test (gallery, lightbox, agent chat, post-creation selection, drag-after-multi-select).
6. **List every test file that will need updating** and what kind of update (mock signature change, behavior assertion change, etc.).

- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: checked how remotion itself acquires delay handles in `node_modules/remotion/dist/cjs/iframe.js:8-18`. remotion's own components create the handle synchronously with `usestate(() => delayrender(...))`; the plan says 'calls delayrender() on mount', which reads like an effect-time action and leaves the initial-frame blocking behavior underspecified compared with the actual library pattern.         Idea:
Structural cleanup of the video-editor selection store API.

# Background

We just landed a 3-line quick fix on branch `megaplan/m1b-m1c-stores` that removes redundant double-writes from `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineSelection.ts`. The wrapper was calling both the store action AND a `setSelectedClipId` pass-through that routed to `setTimelineSelectedClipId` → `selectTimelineClip(id, undefined)`, which silently reset multi-select to single-select. Marquee + cmd+click multi-select are now functional.

The bug is fixed but the underlying smell that produced it is intact: the selection store has three overlapping entry points with subtly-different semantics, one of which (`setTimelineSelectedClipId`) masquerades as a `useState` setter while actually clobbering the whole selection. The wrapper layer (`useTimelineSelection`) still has the pre-refactor "split state" shape (multi-select set + useState-style primary id) even though M1b/M1c collapsed those into a single Zustand store.

# Goal

Eliminate the structural trap permanently so this class of bug cannot reappear, even if a future refactor wires the surfaces back together. This megaplan plans the cleanup ONLY — the bug fix is already applied. The cleanup should ship in the same PR as the quick fix but as a separate commit so the fix is revertable independently.

# Specific objectives

1. **Disambiguate the three entry points** in `src/shared/state/selectionStore.ts`:
   - `selectTimelineClips(set, syncOptions)` — replaces multi-selection
   - `selectTimelineClip(id, opts, syncOptions)` — single or toggle
   - `setTimelineSelectedClipId(updater, options)` — masquerades as primary-id setter, actually resets selection. **THIS IS THE TRAP.**

   Either rename `setTimelineSelectedClipId` so it stops looking like a `useState` setter, or split it into `setPrimaryClipId` (pure primary update, no reset) + `selectSingleClip` (replaces selection with one). Pick whichever leaves the cleanest contract for callers.

2. **Decide the fate of `useTimelineSelection`**. Post-M1b/M1c, the wrapper is a thin layer over the store but still presents `Dispatch<SetStateAction<string | null>>` semantics. Options:
   - Kill it; have callers use the store hooks directly.
   - Thin it to JUST derivations (`selectedClip`, `selectedTrack`, `selectedClipHasPredecessor`, `resolvedConfig` from `useDerivedTimeline`) and drop all selection-mutation methods.

3. **Update `useTimelineCommit.ts:117`**. This is where `setSelectedClipId` is created with the deceptive setState-style signature. It needs to either disappear (callers go direct) or be renamed to match the new contract.

4. **Document semantics inline** so the next refactor doesn't reintroduce the trap. JSDoc on each store action stating exactly what it resets and what it preserves.

# Constraints / context

- **Branch**: `megaplan/m1b-m1c-stores` (not yet merged; itself a major refactor moving selection from React Context into Zustand stores).
- **User confirmed they are happy with churn** — broad renames and call-site updates are acceptable.
- **Test files affected** (~6+): `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipEditing.test.ts`, `src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/ClipAction.test.tsx`, and others mocking `setSelectedClipId: vi.fn()`.

## Adjacent flows the planner MUST check for hidden coupling

These flows touch selection and may rely on the side effects of the current double-write or the setState-style signature. The plan must verify each:

- **Gallery sync** (`clearGallery` options on store actions). Some callers pass `{clearGallery: false}` — if those reach a renamed/split API, the option must survive.
- **Lightbox navigation** — `MediaLightbox` interaction with selection state.
- **Agent chat ops** — `AgentChatContext` and `AgentChat` reference selection (per the modified files in working tree).
- **Programmatic post-creation selection** — select-after-paste, select-after-shot-creation, select-after-clip-duplication. Often uses `setSelectedClipId(newId)` semantics.
- **`useClipDrag` pointer-up** — calls `selectClip(id, {toggle, preserveSelection})` based on modifier keys and touch interaction.
- **`useMarqueeSelect`** — calls `selectClips`, `addToSelection`, `clearSelection`.
- **`useAssetManagement`** — passes `setSelectedClipId` through.

## Files in the surface area (not exhaustive)

- `src/shared/state/selectionStore.ts` — the store (where the renames land)
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineSelection.ts` — the wrapper (kill or thin)
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineCommit.ts:117` — the bridge (likely the surface to rename or remove)
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineState.ts` — composes selection into editor state
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipDrag.ts` — call site
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useMarqueeSelect.ts` — call site
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useAssetManagement.ts` — call site
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipEditing.ts` — call site
- `src/tools/video-editor/contexts/VideoEditorProvider.tsx` — composes ops into the timelineStore
- All test files that mock these APIs

# What I want from this plan

1. **Map the current API surface and EVERY call site** (don't trust my partial list — search the whole repo).
2. **Propose a target API** with exact names and signatures. Justify the choice (split vs single rename).
3. **Sequence the migration into reviewable chunks** — ideally each chunk leaves the build green.
4. **Identify load-bearing side effects** of the current double-write — places where the second write was the actual intended behavior, not a bug.
5. **Identify adjacent-flow verification points** — what to manually test (gallery, lightbox, agent chat, post-creation selection, drag-after-multi-select).
6. **List every test file that will need updating** and what kind of update (mock signature change, behavior assertion change, etc.).

T1 resolves this; do NOT carry the ambiguity past T1.\n\nThe single load-bearing invariant: `useTimelineMultiSelect`'s `{clearGallery: false}` adapter at `selectionStore.ts:780-789` MUST stay. The JSDoc on `clearTimelineSelection` must state this as a 'Note: opposite gallery default' callout \u2014 boilerplate that papers over the divergence would seed the same kind of misreading that produced the original trap. The plan deliberately does NOT normalize this asymmetry; that is a behavior-change PR.\n\n`useTimelineCommit.ts:190` keeps an explicit `{clearGallery: false}` even though it is functionally redundant with `clearTimelineSelection`'s default. Resist 'cleaning up' the redundancy.\n\n`setSelectedTrackId` is the lookalike trap \u2014 it ISN'T a trap because track selection is a single scalar with no multi-select to clobber. Keep it untouched. Do NOT use a broad grep pattern that catches it; use `\\\\bsetSelectedClipId\\\\b` precisely.\n\nOVERLAP_FILES staging is the most failure-prone part of execution.         Idea:
Structural cleanup of the video-editor selection store API.

# Background

We just landed a 3-line quick fix on branch `megaplan/m1b-m1c-stores` that removes redundant double-writes from `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineSelection.ts`. The wrapper was calling both the store action AND a `setSelectedClipId` pass-through that routed to `setTimelineSelectedClipId` → `selectTimelineClip(id, undefined)`, which silently reset multi-select to single-select. Marquee + cmd+click multi-select are now functional.

The bug is fixed but the underlying smell that produced it is intact: the selection store has three overlapping entry points with subtly-different semantics, one of which (`setTimelineSelectedClipId`) masquerades as a `useState` setter while actually clobbering the whole selection. The wrapper layer (`useTimelineSelection`) still has the pre-refactor "split state" shape (multi-select set + useState-style primary id) even though M1b/M1c collapsed those into a single Zustand store.

# Goal

Eliminate the structural trap permanently so this class of bug cannot reappear, even if a future refactor wires the surfaces back together. This megaplan plans the cleanup ONLY — the bug fix is already applied. The cleanup should ship in the same PR as the quick fix but as a separate commit so the fix is revertable independently.

# Specific objectives

1. **Disambiguate the three entry points** in `src/shared/state/selectionStore.ts`:
   - `selectTimelineClips(set, syncOptions)` — replaces multi-selection
   - `selectTimelineClip(id, opts, syncOptions)` — single or toggle
   - `setTimelineSelectedClipId(updater, options)` — masquerades as primary-id setter, actually resets selection. **THIS IS THE TRAP.**

   Either rename `setTimelineSelectedClipId` so it stops looking like a `useState` setter, or split it into `setPrimaryClipId` (pure primary update, no reset) + `selectSingleClip` (replaces selection with one). Pick whichever leaves the cleanest contract for callers.

2. **Decide the fate of `useTimelineSelection`**. Post-M1b/M1c, the wrapper is a thin layer over the store but still presents `Dispatch<SetStateAction<string | null>>` semantics. Options:
   - Kill it; have callers use the store hooks directly.
   - Thin it to JUST derivations (`selectedClip`, `selectedTrack`, `selectedClipHasPredecessor`, `resolvedConfig` from `useDerivedTimeline`) and drop all selection-mutation methods.

3. **Update `useTimelineCommit.ts:117`**. This is where `setSelectedClipId` is created with the deceptive setState-style signature. It needs to either disappear (callers go direct) or be renamed to match the new contract.

4. **Document semantics inline** so the next refactor doesn't reintroduce the trap. JSDoc on each store action stating exactly what it resets and what it preserves.

# Constraints / context

- **Branch**: `megaplan/m1b-m1c-stores` (not yet merged; itself a major refactor moving selection from React Context into Zustand stores).
- **User confirmed they are happy with churn** — broad renames and call-site updates are acceptable.
- **Test files affected** (~6+): `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipEditing.test.ts`, `src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/ClipAction.test.tsx`, and others mocking `setSelectedClipId: vi.fn()`.

## Adjacent flows the planner MUST check for hidden coupling

These flows touch selection and may rely on the side effects of the current double-write or the setState-style signature. The plan must verify each:

- **Gallery sync** (`clearGallery` options on store actions). Some callers pass `{clearGallery: false}` — if those reach a renamed/split API, the option must survive.
- **Lightbox navigation** — `MediaLightbox` interaction with selection state.
- **Agent chat ops** — `AgentChatContext` and `AgentChat` reference selection (per the modified files in working tree).
- **Programmatic post-creation selection** — select-after-paste, select-after-shot-creation, select-after-clip-duplication. Often uses `setSelectedClipId(newId)` semantics.
- **`useClipDrag` pointer-up** — calls `selectClip(id, {toggle, preserveSelection})` based on modifier keys and touch interaction.
- **`useMarqueeSelect`** — calls `selectClips`, `addToSelection`, `clearSelection`.
- **`useAssetManagement`** — passes `setSelectedClipId` through.

## Files in the surface area (not exhaustive)

- `src/shared/state/selectionStore.ts` — the store (where the renames land)
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineSelection.ts` — the wrapper (kill or thin)
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineCommit.ts:117` — the bridge (likely the surface to rename or remove)
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineState.ts` — composes selection into editor state
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipDrag.ts` — call site
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useMarqueeSelect.ts` — call site
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useAssetManagement.ts` — call site
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipEditing.ts` — call site
- `src/tools/video-editor/contexts/VideoEditorProvider.tsx` — composes ops into the timelineStore
- All test files that mock these APIs

# What I want from this plan

1. **Map the current API surface and EVERY call site** (don't trust my partial list — search the whole repo).
2. **Propose a target API** with exact names and signatures. Justify the choice (split vs single rename).
3. **Sequence the migration into reviewable chunks** — ideally each chunk leaves the build green.
4. **Identify load-bearing side effects** of the current double-write — places where the second write was the actual intended behavior, not a bug.
5. **Identify adjacent-flow verification points** — what to manually test (gallery, lightbox, agent chat, post-creation selection, drag-after-multi-select).
6. **List every test file that will need updating** and what kind of update (mock signature change, behavior assertion change, etc.).

T1 resolves this; do NOT carry the ambiguity past T1.\n\nThe single load-bearing invariant: `useTimelineMultiSelect`'s `{clearGallery: false}` adapter at `selectionStore.ts:780-789` MUST stay.         Idea:
Structural cleanup of the video-editor selection store API.

# Background

We just landed a 3-line quick fix on branch `megaplan/m1b-m1c-stores` that removes redundant double-writes from `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineSelection.ts`. The wrapper was calling both the store action AND a `setSelectedClipId` pass-through that routed to `setTimelineSelectedClipId` → `selectTimelineClip(id, undefined)`, which silently reset multi-select to single-select. Marquee + cmd+click multi-select are now functional.

The bug is fixed but the underlying smell that produced it is intact: the selection store has three overlapping entry points with subtly-different semantics, one of which (`setTimelineSelectedClipId`) masquerades as a `useState` setter while actually clobbering the whole selection. The wrapper layer (`useTimelineSelection`) still has the pre-refactor "split state" shape (multi-select set + useState-style primary id) even though M1b/M1c collapsed those into a single Zustand store.

# Goal

Eliminate the structural trap permanently so this class of bug cannot reappear, even if a future refactor wires the surfaces back together. This megaplan plans the cleanup ONLY — the bug fix is already applied. The cleanup should ship in the same PR as the quick fix but as a separate commit so the fix is revertable independently.

# Specific objectives

1. **Disambiguate the three entry points** in `src/shared/state/selectionStore.ts`:
   - `selectTimelineClips(set, syncOptions)` — replaces multi-selection
   - `selectTimelineClip(id, opts, syncOptions)` — single or toggle
   - `setTimelineSelectedClipId(updater, options)` — masquerades as primary-id setter, actually resets selection. **THIS IS THE TRAP.**

   Either rename `setTimelineSelectedClipId` so it stops looking like a `useState` setter, or split it into `setPrimaryClipId` (pure primary update, no reset) + `selectSingleClip` (replaces selection with one). Pick whichever leaves the cleanest contract for callers.

2. **Decide the fate of `useTimelineSelection`**. Post-M1b/M1c, the wrapper is a thin layer over the store but still presents `Dispatch<SetStateAction<string | null>>` semantics. Options:
   - Kill it; have callers use the store hooks directly.
   - Thin it to JUST derivations (`selectedClip`, `selectedTrack`, `selectedClipHasPredecessor`, `resolvedConfig` from `useDerivedTimeline`) and drop all selection-mutation methods.

3. **Update `useTimelineCommit.ts:117`**. This is where `setSelectedClipId` is created with the deceptive setState-style signature. It needs to either disappear (callers go direct) or be renamed to match the new contract.

4. **Document semantics inline** so the next refactor doesn't reintroduce the trap. JSDoc on each store action stating exactly what it resets and what it preserves.

# Constraints / context

- **Branch**: `megaplan/m1b-m1c-stores` (not yet merged; itself a major refactor moving selection from React Context into Zustand stores).
- **User confirmed they are happy with churn** — broad renames and call-site updates are acceptable.
- **Test files affected** (~6+): `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipEditing.test.ts`, `src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/ClipAction.test.tsx`, and others mocking `setSelectedClipId: vi.fn()`.

## Adjacent flows the planner MUST check for hidden coupling

These flows touch selection and may rely on the side effects of the current double-write or the setState-style signature. The plan must verify each:

- **Gallery sync** (`clearGallery` options on store actions). Some callers pass `{clearGallery: false}` — if those reach a renamed/split API, the option must survive.
- **Lightbox navigation** — `MediaLightbox` interaction with selection state.
- **Agent chat ops** — `AgentChatContext` and `AgentChat` reference selection (per the modified files in working tree).
- **Programmatic post-creation selection** — select-after-paste, select-after-shot-creation, select-after-clip-duplication. Often uses `setSelectedClipId(newId)` semantics.
- **`useClipDrag` pointer-up** — calls `selectClip(id, {toggle, preserveSelection})` based on modifier keys and touch interaction.
- **`useMarqueeSelect`** — calls `selectClips`, `addToSelection`, `clearSelection`.
- **`useAssetManagement`** — passes `setSelectedClipId` through.

## Files in the surface area (not exhaustive)

- `src/shared/state/selectionStore.ts` — the store (where the renames land)
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineSelection.ts` — the wrapper (kill or thin)
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineCommit.ts:117` — the bridge (likely the surface to rename or remove)
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineState.ts` — composes selection into editor state
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipDrag.ts` — call site
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useMarqueeSelect.ts` — call site
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useAssetManagement.ts` — call site
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipEditing.ts` — call site
- `src/tools/video-editor/contexts/VideoEditorProvider.tsx` — composes ops into the timelineStore
- All test files that mock these APIs

# What I want from this plan

1. **Map the current API surface and EVERY call site** (don't trust my partial list — search the whole repo).
2. **Propose a target API** with exact names and signatures. Justify the choice (split vs single rename).
3. **Sequence the migration into reviewable chunks** — ideally each chunk leaves the build green.
4. **Identify load-bearing side effects** of the current double-write — places where the second write was the actual intended behavior, not a bug.
5. **Identify adjacent-flow verification points** — what to manually test (gallery, lightbox, agent chat, post-creation selection, drag-after-multi-select).
6. **List every test file that will need updating** and what kind of update (mock signature change, behavior assertion change, etc.).

T1 resolves this; do NOT carry the ambiguity past T1.\n\nThe single load-bearing invariant: `useTimelineMultiSelect`'s `{clearGallery: false}` adapter at `selectionStore.ts:780-789` MUST stay. It preserves gallery selection during editor-internal mutations (drag, marquee, programmatic post-creation selects). The cleanup ONLY removes the trap method (`setSelectedClipId` field on the hook surface and the underlying `setTimelineSelectedClipId` action) \u2014 not the surrounding wrappers. If the post-cleanup smoke shows that clicking a timeline clip clears gallery selection, T2 was misapplied (the adapter was deleted with the trap).\n\nThe most subtle correctness point is the gallery-default asymmetry: `clearTimelineSelection` PRESERVES gallery by default (opt-IN to clear), opposite to `selectTimelineClip`/`selectTimelineClips` which CLEAR gallery by default (opt-OUT). The JSDoc on `clearTimelineSelection` must state this as a 'Note: opposite gallery default' callout \u2014 boilerplate that papers over the divergence would seed the same kind of misreading that produced the original trap. The plan deliberately does NOT normalize this asymmetry; that is a behavior-change PR.\n\n`useTimelineCommit.ts:190` keeps an explicit `{clearGallery: false}` even though it is functionally redundant with `clearTimelineSelection`'s default. This is intentional readability \u2014 a reader scanning the commit hook sees the same `{clearGallery: false}` keyword on every editor-internal selection write. Resist 'cleaning up' the redundancy.\n\n`setSelectedTrackId` is the lookalike trap \u2014 it ISN'T a trap because track selection is a single scalar with no multi-select to clobber. Keep it untouched. Do NOT use a broad grep pattern that catches it; use `\\\\bsetSelectedClipId\\\\b` precisely.\n\nOVERLAP_FILES staging is the most failure-prone part of execution. The user is mid-stream on a pane-refactor bakeoff with entangled changes across many files; `git stash` is NOT safe here. Use `git add -p <path>` for every overlap file, then `git diff --cached -- <path>` per overlap file before commit. If foreign hunks slip in, `git restore --staged <path>` and redo. The path-only `git status --short` check is necessary but insufficient \u2014 the per-overlap-file diff review is the load-bearing protection.\n\n`useAssetManagement.ts` is easy to half-migrate. The prop AND the store-backed resolver (`getSetSelectedClipId` \u2192 `getSelectClip` reading `ops.selectClip`) MUST move together. Missing the store-backed path silently breaks post-paste / post-creation selection at runtime even though the build passes.\n\nValidation cadence (matches plan): tsc after T4 (Phase 1-2 done), tsc after T8 (Phase 4 done), tsc after T11 (Phase 5 done), then full vitest + grep + manual smoke after T12. Do not skip the intermediate tsc runs \u2014 they catch broken consumers cheaply before the test suite has to.",

(flagged 2 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: checked the render-gating cleanup plan against remotion's runtime exports in `node_modules/remotion/dist/cjs/cancel-render.js:46-70`. `cancelrender()` stores an error and throws to abort the render; it is not a benign cleanup for an abandoned `delayrender` handle, so step 2's instruction to call `cancelrender(handle)` on unmount is technically wrong and would abort preview or export with an error. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: checked how remotion itself acquires delay handles in `node_modules/remotion/dist/cjs/iframe.js:8-18`. remotion's own components create the handle synchronously with `usestate(() => delayrender(...))`; the plan says 'calls delayrender() on mount', which reads like an effect-time action and leaves the initial-frame blocking behavior underspecified compared with the actual library pattern. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: checked the new `useaudioparam()` sketch against `src/tools/video-editor/effects/compileeffect.tsx:1-2`. the plan defines it in terms of `interpolate(audio[binding.source], ...)` but does not explicitly import `interpolate` into the new hook file or simplify it to straight arithmetic, so the helper's implementation contract is still looser than it needs to be.         Idea:
Structural cleanup of the video-editor selection store API.

# Background

We just landed a 3-line quick fix on branch `megaplan/m1b-m1c-stores` that removes redundant double-writes from `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineSelection.ts`. The wrapper was calling both the store action AND a `setSelectedClipId` pass-through that routed to `setTimelineSelectedClipId` → `selectTimelineClip(id, undefined)`, which silently reset multi-select to single-select. Marquee + cmd+click multi-select are now functional.

The bug is fixed but the underlying smell that produced it is intact: the selection store has three overlapping entry points with subtly-different semantics, one of which (`setTimelineSelectedClipId`) masquerades as a `useState` setter while actually clobbering the whole selection. The wrapper layer (`useTimelineSelection`) still has the pre-refactor "split state" shape (multi-select set + useState-style primary id) even though M1b/M1c collapsed those into a single Zustand store.

# Goal

Eliminate the structural trap permanently so this class of bug cannot reappear, even if a future refactor wires the surfaces back together. This megaplan plans the cleanup ONLY — the bug fix is already applied. The cleanup should ship in the same PR as the quick fix but as a separate commit so the fix is revertable independently.

# Specific objectives

1. **Disambiguate the three entry points** in `src/shared/state/selectionStore.ts`:
   - `selectTimelineClips(set, syncOptions)` — replaces multi-selection
   - `selectTimelineClip(id, opts, syncOptions)` — single or toggle
   - `setTimelineSelectedClipId(updater, options)` — masquerades as primary-id setter, actually resets selection. **THIS IS THE TRAP.**

   Either rename `setTimelineSelectedClipId` so it stops looking like a `useState` setter, or split it into `setPrimaryClipId` (pure primary update, no reset) + `selectSingleClip` (replaces selection with one). Pick whichever leaves the cleanest contract for callers.

2. **Decide the fate of `useTimelineSelection`**. Post-M1b/M1c, the wrapper is a thin layer over the store but still presents `Dispatch<SetStateAction<string | null>>` semantics. Options:
   - Kill it; have callers use the store hooks directly.
   - Thin it to JUST derivations (`selectedClip`, `selectedTrack`, `selectedClipHasPredecessor`, `resolvedConfig` from `useDerivedTimeline`) and drop all selection-mutation methods.

3. **Update `useTimelineCommit.ts:117`**. This is where `setSelectedClipId` is created with the deceptive setState-style signature. It needs to either disappear (callers go direct) or be renamed to match the new contract.

4. **Document semantics inline** so the next refactor doesn't reintroduce the trap. JSDoc on each store action stating exactly what it resets and what it preserves.

# Constraints / context

- **Branch**: `megaplan/m1b-m1c-stores` (not yet merged; itself a major refactor moving selection from React Context into Zustand stores).
- **User confirmed they are happy with churn** — broad renames and call-site updates are acceptable.
- **Test files affected** (~6+): `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipEditing.test.ts`, `src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/ClipAction.test.tsx`, and others mocking `setSelectedClipId: vi.fn()`.

## Adjacent flows the planner MUST check for hidden coupling

These flows touch selection and may rely on the side effects of the current double-write or the setState-style signature. The plan must verify each:

- **Gallery sync** (`clearGallery` options on store actions). Some callers pass `{clearGallery: false}` — if those reach a renamed/split API, the option must survive.
- **Lightbox navigation** — `MediaLightbox` interaction with selection state.
- **Agent chat ops** — `AgentChatContext` and `AgentChat` reference selection (per the modified files in working tree).
- **Programmatic post-creation selection** — select-after-paste, select-after-shot-creation, select-after-clip-duplication. Often uses `setSelectedClipId(newId)` semantics.
- **`useClipDrag` pointer-up** — calls `selectClip(id, {toggle, preserveSelection})` based on modifier keys and touch interaction.
- **`useMarqueeSelect`** — calls `selectClips`, `addToSelection`, `clearSelection`.
- **`useAssetManagement`** — passes `setSelectedClipId` through.

## Files in the surface area (not exhaustive)

- `src/shared/state/selectionStore.ts` — the store (where the renames land)
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineSelection.ts` — the wrapper (kill or thin)
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineCommit.ts:117` — the bridge (likely the surface to rename or remove)
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineState.ts` — composes selection into editor state
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipDrag.ts` — call site
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useMarqueeSelect.ts` — call site
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useAssetManagement.ts` — call site
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipEditing.ts` — call site
- `src/tools/video-editor/contexts/VideoEditorProvider.tsx` — composes ops into the timelineStore
- All test files that mock these APIs

# What I want from this plan

1. **Map the current API surface and EVERY call site** (don't trust my partial list — search the whole repo).
2. **Propose a target API** with exact names and signatures. Justify the choice (split vs single rename).
3. **Sequence the migration into reviewable chunks** — ideally each chunk leaves the build green.

5. **Identify adjacent-flow verification points** — what to manually test (gallery, lightbox, agent chat, post-creation selection, drag-after-multi-select).
6. **List every test file that will need updating** and what kind of update (mock signature change, behavior assertion change, etc.).

  "meta_commentary": "This cleanup ships in TWO commits on `megaplan/m1b-m1c-stores`: (1) the 3-line bug fix `fix(selection): remove double-write that clobbers multi-select` and (2) the structural cleanup `refactor(selection): remove setTimelineSelectedClipId trap`. Either may already exist (State A) or both may be in the worktree (State B). T1 resolves this; do NOT carry the ambiguity past T1.\n\nThe single load-bearing invariant: `useTimelineMultiSelect`'s `{clearGallery: false}` adapter at `selectionStore.ts:780-789` MUST stay. It preserves gallery selection during editor-internal mutations (drag, marquee, programmatic post-creation selects). The cleanup ONLY removes the trap method (`setSelectedClipId` field on the hook surface and the underlying `setTimelineSelectedClipId` action) \u2014 not the surrounding wrappers. If the post-cleanup smoke shows that clicking a timeline clip clears gallery selection, T2 was misapplied (the adapter was deleted with the trap).\n\nThe most subtle correctness point is the gallery-default asymmetry: `clearTimelineSelection` PRESERVES gallery by default (opt-IN to clear), opposite to `selectTimelineClip`/`selectTimelineClips` which CLEAR gallery by default (opt-OUT). The JSDoc on `clearTimelineSelection` must state this as a 'Note: opposite gallery default' callout \u2014 boilerplate that papers over the divergence would seed the same kind of misreading that produced the original trap. The plan deliberately does NOT normalize this asymmetry; that is a behavior-change PR.\n\n`useTimelineCommit.ts:190` keeps an explicit `{clearGallery: false}` even though it is functionally redundant with `clearTimelineSelection`'s default. This is intentional readability \u2014 a reader scanning the commit hook sees the same `{clearGallery: false}` keyword on every editor-internal selection write. Resist 'cleaning up' the redundancy.\n\n`setSelectedTrackId` is the lookalike trap \u2014 it ISN'T a trap because track selection is a single scalar with no multi-select to clobber. Keep it untouched. Do NOT use a broad grep pattern that catches it; use `\\\\bsetSelectedClipId\\\\b` precisely.\n\nOVERLAP_FILES staging is the most failure-prone part of execution. The user is mid-stream on a pane-refactor bakeoff with entangled changes across many files; `git stash` is NOT safe here. Use `git add -p <path>` for every overlap file, then `git diff --cached -- <path>` per overlap file before commit. If foreign hunks slip in, `git restore --staged <path>` and redo. The path-only `git status --short` check is necessary but insufficient \u2014 the per-overlap-file diff review is the load-bearing protection.\n\n`useAssetManagement.ts` is easy to half-migrate. The prop AND the store-backed resolver (`getSetSelectedClipId` \u2192 `getSelectClip` reading `ops.selectClip`) MUST move together. Missing the store-backed path silently breaks post-paste / post-creation selection at runtime even though the build passes.\n\nValidation cadence (matches plan): tsc after T4 (Phase 1-2 done), tsc after T8 (Phase 4 done), tsc after T11 (Phase 5 done), then full vitest + grep + manual smoke after T12. Do not skip the intermediate tsc runs \u2014 they catch broken consumers cheaply before the test suite has to.",

        Idea:
Structural cleanup of the video-editor selection store API.

# Background

We just landed a 3-line quick fix on branch `megaplan/m1b-m1c-stores` that removes redundant double-writes from `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineSelection.ts`. The wrapper was calling both the store action AND a `setSelectedClipId` pass-through that routed to `setTimelineSelectedClipId` → `selectTimelineClip(id, undefined)`, which silently reset multi-select to single-select. Marquee + cmd+click multi-select are now functional.

The bug is fixed but the underlying smell that produced it is intact: the selection store has three overlapping entry points with subtly-different semantics, one of which (`setTimelineSelectedClipId`) masquerades as a `useState` setter while actually clobbering the whole selection. The wrapper layer (`useTimelineSelection`) still has the pre-refactor "split state" shape (multi-select set + useState-style primary id) even though M1b/M1c collapsed those into a single Zustand store.

# Goal

Eliminate the structural trap permanently so this class of bug cannot reappear, even if a future refactor wires the surfaces back together. This megaplan plans the cleanup ONLY — the bug fix is already applied. The cleanup should ship in the same PR as the quick fix but as a separate commit so the fix is revertable independently.

# Specific objectives

1. **Disambiguate the three entry points** in `src/shared/state/selectionStore.ts`:
   - `selectTimelineClips(set, syncOptions)` — replaces multi-selection
   - `selectTimelineClip(id, opts, syncOptions)` — single or toggle
   - `setTimelineSelectedClipId(updater, options)` — masquerades as primary-id setter, actually resets selection. **THIS IS THE TRAP.**

   Either rename `setTimelineSelectedClipId` so it stops looking like a `useState` setter, or split it into `setPrimaryClipId` (pure primary update, no reset) + `selectSingleClip` (replaces selection with one). Pick whichever leaves the cleanest contract for callers.

2. **Decide the fate of `useTimelineSelection`**. Post-M1b/M1c, the wrapper is a thin layer over the store but still presents `Dispatch<SetStateAction<string | null>>` semantics. Options:
   - Kill it; have callers use the store hooks directly.
   - Thin it to JUST derivations (`selectedClip`, `selectedTrack`, `selectedClipHasPredecessor`, `resolvedConfig` from `useDerivedTimeline`) and drop all selection-mutation methods.

3. **Update `useTimelineCommit.ts:117`**. This is where `setSelectedClipId` is created with the deceptive setState-style signature. It needs to either disappear (callers go direct) or be renamed to match the new contract.

4. **Document semantics inline** so the next refactor doesn't reintroduce the trap. JSDoc on each store action stating exactly what it resets and what it preserves.

# Constraints / context

- **Branch**: `megaplan/m1b-m1c-stores` (not yet merged; itself a major refactor moving selection from React Context into Zustand stores).
- **User confirmed they are happy with churn** — broad renames and call-site updates are acceptable.
- **Test files affected** (~6+): `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipEditing.test.ts`, `src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/ClipAction.test.tsx`, and others mocking `setSelectedClipId: vi.fn()`.

## Adjacent flows the planner MUST check for hidden coupling

These flows touch selection and may rely on the side effects of the current double-write or the setState-style signature. The plan must verify each:

- **Gallery sync** (`clearGallery` options on store actions). Some callers pass `{clearGallery: false}` — if those reach a renamed/split API, the option must survive.
- **Lightbox navigation** — `MediaLightbox` interaction with selection state.
- **Agent chat ops** — `AgentChatContext` and `AgentChat` reference selection (per the modified files in working tree).
- **Programmatic post-creation selection** — select-after-paste, select-after-shot-creation, select-after-clip-duplication. Often uses `setSelectedClipId(newId)` semantics.
- **`useClipDrag` pointer-up** — calls `selectClip(id, {toggle, preserveSelection})` based on modifier keys and touch interaction.
- **`useMarqueeSelect`** — calls `selectClips`, `addToSelection`, `clearSelection`.
- **`useAssetManagement`** — passes `setSelectedClipId` through.

## Files in the surface area (not exhaustive)

- `src/shared/state/selectionStore.ts` — the store (where the renames land)
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineSelection.ts` — the wrapper (kill or thin)
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineCommit.ts:117` — the bridge (likely the surface to rename or remove)
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineState.ts` — composes selection into editor state
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipDrag.ts` — call site
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useMarqueeSelect.ts` — call site
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useAssetManagement.ts` — call site
- `src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipEditing.ts` — call site
- `src/tools/video-editor/contexts/VideoEditorProvider.tsx` — composes ops into the timelineStore
- All test files that mock these APIs

# What I want from this plan

3. **Sequence the migration into reviewable chunks** — ideally each chunk leaves the build green.

5. **Identify adjacent-flow verification points** — what to manually test (gallery, lightbox, agent chat, post-creation selection, drag-after-multi-select).
6. **List every test file that will need updating** and what kind of update (mock signature change, behavior assertion change, etc.).
